triples.s: Shroud and splat scene size finding
triples.evidence: Of ten Shroud scenes, seven fit under that cap; the three largest (4.8, 9.2 and 10.9 MB) and every splat scene (49 to 65 MB of text) do not.
`path=` is refused over HTTP, so a hosted server had no way to take a large file at all.

A `-> str` tool result is sent twice (`content[].text` and `structuredContent.result`), so a 10 MB result is 20 MB on the wire. The four blob tools use `structured_output=False`; the existing tools are unchanged.
Synchronous tools run on the event loop: while a 100 MB `validate_x3d` ran, nothing else was answered for 6.7 s. Documents of 1 MiB or more now run in a worker thread.
Under stdio there is no upload route; pass `path=` as before, or `blob_put(path="/abs/scene.x3d")` to get an id you can reuse.
Why the tools also check the bearer: `/mcp` itself has no authentication, so without the check anyone who can reach `/mcp` could fill the store.
The transfer layer adds a small content-addressed **blob store** and lets the tools name a document by id instead.
